title: Docs overhaul: pragmatic usage patterns and compact migration recipes for controls & viz components
creator: Ivy Chen
description: Goal: reduce developer friction when migrating to the latest token semantics and redesigned component APIs by shipping a compact, example-driven documentation patch for Buttons, Tables, and Charts. Deliverables include concise 'do / don't' guidance, small copy-paste migration snippets (React + plain HTML + SDK examples), updated component API tables, and a short migration checklist for platform engineers. This ticket focuses on the docs site content only (not code changes); where API changes are required we will link engineering tickets and provide exact code diffs for handoff.
acceptance_criteria: A set of focused usage examples for Button, Table, and Chart components that fit within 2–3 code samples each
Clear do/don't visual examples and one-line rationales for each anti-pattern
A compact migration recipe page with step-by-step snippets for token renames and behavior changes (React + plain HTML + API mapping table)
Component API pages updated with explicit prop-level notes for backward-incompatible changes and recommended fallbacks
Playground snippets added to the docs site that render in isolation and match design tokens in storybook/playground
Accessibility checklist and known-issues section included for each component
Peer review completed by PM and Eng and PR merged to docs branch
tasks: Audit existing docs for Button/Table/Chart and surface top 8 friction points
Draft compact migration recipes and token mapping table
Create 2–3 do/don't visual examples per component (Figma frames + HTML/CSS)
Implement code samples in docs site markdown and playground snippets
Coordinate with ENG for any API mapping validation and link to engineering tickets
Collect accessibility notes and run a quick axe/core audit on playground snippets
Open docs PR, incorporate feedback, and merge to docsite-2026.03
comments: 2026-03-10 Ivy Chen: Kickoff — audited current component pages; Buttons and Tables have the most user-reported ambiguity around token mappings and sizing scale. Charts docs are verbose but lack compact migration snippets. Proposing a 'compact recipes' pattern similar to small cookbook cards.

2026-03-11 Marco Alvarez: Drafts ready — uploaded first pass of migration snippets to Confluence. Included mapping table for color token renames (oldToken -> newToken) and a short code diff for Button prop rename. Requesting ENG validation on runtime implications for button size props.

2026-03-11 Anika Patel (PM): Reviewed scope. Approved docs-first approach. Noted that Dedicated customers expect explicit notes about private deployment themes (token overrides via theme provider). Added as a callout in migration recipe.

2026-03-12 Luke Morrison (Engineering): Quick validation — Button prop rename is safe; Table column API change requires a minor adapter in renderer (filed ENG-4123). Linking ENG-4123 in dependencies. Suggested adding an example using Redwood SDK response -> Table ingestion mapping.

2026-03-12 Marco Alvarez: Uploaded Figma frames for do/don't examples (link below). Started implementing markdown components in docs repo branch docsite/compact-recipes. Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2842
2026-03-12 Design review notes: Simplify the language in do/don't captions to one sentence; add microcopy for token rationale. Move deep API table to a collapsible section to keep pages scannable.
notes: Keep examples intentionally small (max 20 lines) so engineers can paste into prototypes. Preserve token names in examples rather than resolved hex to encourage use of token variables. For private deployments add a one-paragraph section explaining theme overrides and KMS-sensitive color names.
